transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-28 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM), Jon (Vela Head of InfoSec), Mark (Vela Cloud Architect), Riya (Vela Procurement)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Vela's vendor security questionnaire (mix of SIG/CAIQ and customer-specific items). Focus on SOC 2, RBAC/SSO, audit logs retention and format, KMS/encryption, and data residency options. Agreed to share SOC 2 report and sample logs; Redwood to map SIG responses in spreadsheet and follow up.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and periods
- ISO timeline and scope
- SSO/SAML + Okta integration and RBAC model
- Audit log retention, format, and export (CSV/JSON examples)
- Encryption at rest and KMS / HSM details
- Data residency (US/EU) and Private deployment options
- SIG/CAIQ artifacts and packaging of evidence

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i, uh, we'll keep this tight, we got about 55 minutes. quick intros?
[00:00:12] Jon (Vela): jon here, head of infosec at vela, i'll own the questionnaire on our side.
[00:00:16] Mark (Vela): mark, cloud architect, i'll be the tech contact.
[00:00:20] Riya (Vela): hi, riya from procurement, i'll track timeline and PO.
[00:00:25] Priya: great. samir from our se team is on to field the deeper tech questions. samir?
[00:00:30] Samir (Redwood SE): hey, thanks. quick note: i've got the SIG we're' — we have a prefilled sheet that maps controls to evidence, i'll walk the heavy ones.
[00:00:40] Jon: perfect. so first big ask — SOC 2. our vendor risk team needs a Type II for the last 12 months, plus the control testing period. can you confirm?
[00:00:50] Priya: yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II for period feb 2024 - jan 2025, report is audit firm 'Harper & Rowe' — i'll upload a redacted copy. full report includes complementary user-entity controls section, and our control mapping.
[00:01:06] Mark: is there an ISO 27001 cert in place?
[00:01:10] Samir: no ISO yet, we are in stage 2 readiness and plan to submit for cert in q1 2026 — we call that out in the SIG responses, but we can't produce a cert today.
[00:01:20] Jon: ok that's fine as long as roadmap is documented. next, encryption: at-rest and in-transit — are keys customer-managed?
[00:01:30] Priya: default is platform-managed KMS keys, AES-256 at-rest and TLS1.2+ in transit. we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for our Private and Dedicated deployments. for hosted tenants, CMK is available as an enterprise add-on.
[00:01:52] Mark: do you use an HSM-backed KMS? we need assurance about key lifecycle.
[00:01:58] Samir: yes, when customers opt for CMKs we use HSM-backed KMS providers (AWS KMS w/ cloudhsm under the hood for AWS). we can provide a KMS architecture diagram and key rotation policies.
[00:02:10] [00:02:12] Jon: audit logs — format and retention? our team wants 12 months, but default looks shorter in your docs.
[00:02:20] Priya: out of the box we keep structured audit logs for 90 days, full export available on request. Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention longer — 12 or 24 months is a common configuration. logs are JSON-line format with timestamp, request id, user id (pseudonymized on export), model, tokens, route, and response metadata.
[00:02:45] Mark: can we get a sample log extract with pseudonymized IDs?
[00:02:48] Samir: yes — action item, i'll export a sample and remove PII. we'll include a mapping file for fields.
[00:02:55] Riya: are logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of custody statements.
[00:03:01] Samir: we sign log bundles with an internal HMAC and maintain immutable storage for archived logs in dedicated accounts, plus we can provide attestations. i'll add the specifics to the evidence pack.
[00:03:12] [00:03:15] Jon: RBAC and SSO: we use okta org-wide. how do you integrate and what granularity?
[00:03:21] Priya: supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC. we recommend SCIM for provisioning to sync groups and then map groups to roles inside Redwood (admin, developer, viewer). roles are enforced at the token layer.
[00:03:36] Samir: small caveat — for dedicated/private we can do full SCIM with SSO, for hosted we provide managed SSO but SCIM provisioning requires enterprise plan.
[00:03:45] Jon: okay, what's the role model — can we define custom roles?
[00:03:48] Samir: yes, custom roles via the console API, but exported as role bindings. We'll provide the RBAC model documentation.
[00:03:55] [00:04:00] Riya: procurement will need a copy of your TLS cert rotation policy and where the CA roots are stored.
[00:04:05] Priya: i'll include cert rotation cadence in the pack — we rotate certs every 12 months and short-lived leaf certs for edge components; root CA handling is with our CA provider, details in the security whitepaper.
[00:04:16] [00:04:20] Mark: data residency — we need EU-only processing for some customers. is region pinning available?
[00:04:25] Samir: yes — region pinning is supported. hosted EU region keeps data and logs in eu-west and we ingest keys in region if CMK required. for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private deployed in your VPC or our dedicated EU zone.
[00:04:40] Jon: do you offer on-prem full air-gapped installation?
[00:04:43] Priya: we have an on-prem package as part of Private, but it's heavier — typically reserved for regulated banks. we can provide an architecture summary, but timeline and costs differ.
[00:04:55] [00:04:58] Riya: the SIG has a bunch of questions about incident response and notification SLA. what's your standard?
[00:05:03] Samir: incident response follows our IR runbook; critical incidents have 1 hour detection/acknowledge SLA, customers get post-incident reports within 72 hours, and we maintain a public status page and private incident channel for enterprise.
[00:05:16] Jon: do you provide breach notification timelines for customers with PII exposure?
[00:05:20] Priya: yes we commit to notify affected customers within our contractual obligations — typically 72 hours after determination, with regular updates.
[00:05:27] [00:05:30] Mark: in the SIG mapping, how do you attach evidence — are you supplying screenshots, configs, audit extracts?
[00:05:36] Samir: we attach evidence as PDFs and redacted logs, architecture diagrams (PNG/PDF), config snippets (yaml) and policy documents. we also include pointer links in the spreadsheet so your security team can validate.
[00:05:48] Priya: note — some SIG fields are auto-filled with references to our security whitepaper and SOC 2 sections, but we leave comments where a manual review is needed.
[00:05:58] [00:06:05] Jon: a few of our questions are around model traceability — how do you track model versions and prompts for audit?
[00:06:12] Samir: requests have model_version metadata and a request hash stored in the audit log. KV/cache layers are not stored in logs, but we keep model config and rollout history in our control plane. we can export a change history for a given model id.
[00:06:30] Jon: great. also, do you allow data deletion requests and what is your retention policy?
[00:06:35] Priya: we support deletion on request; default user-data retention is 90 days for hosted. Dedicated/Private can extend or set custom policies; we will provide the deletion workflow and timelines in the evidence pack.
[00:06:48] [00:06:55] Riya: procurement question — what commercial commitments for security do you offer? any SOC 2-backed SLA credits?
[00:07:02] Priya: we include security attestations and support for evidence; SLA credits are available for Dedicated contracts. procurement and legal can review standard language — i'll flag our legal contact.
[00:07:12] [00:07:20] Mark: one more tech nit — do you run model inference on shared GPUs for hosted tenants? we need noisy-neighbor guarantees.
[00:07:26] Samir: hosted is multi-tenant on optimized runtime with process-level isolation and memory partitioning; Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools for stronger guarantees. we also automatically fallback to smaller model variants to keep latency predictable.
[00:07:44] Jon: are encryption keys rotated automatically?
[00:07:47] Samir: yes, platform keys rotate every 90 days, customer-managed keys follow customer KMS policies; rotation metadata is stored in key control plane.
[00:07:56] [00:08:00] Priya: ok let's talk SIG next steps — we'll send a prefilled spreadsheet, highlight the high-priority rows where you asked for artifacts, and attach SOC 2 and a whitepaper.
[00:08:12] Jon: good. any blockers on our side? we might push for 12 month log retention — is that feasible?
[00:08:18] Samir: totally feasible for Dedicated — for hosted we'd need an enterprise add-on but it's doable; we'll call out any cost impacts in the follow-up.
[00:08:26] [00:08:30] Riya: timeline — procurement wants to close by end of nov if we can get evidence by first week of nov.
[00:08:36] Priya: sounds doable. we'll target SOC2 upload by 2025-11-03 and the log sample and KMS diagram by 2025-11-05.
[00:08:45] [00:08:50] Jon: last question: do you have penetration test reports?
[00:08:53] Samir: yes, annual pentest, last was august 2025 — we can share an executive summary and remediation tracker — full reports are redacted for vendor sharing but we include summary findings and mitigation timelines.
[00:09:06] Priya: ok let's capture action items — i'll email the SIG spreadsheet and SOC2, samir will deliver logs and diagrams, elena will schedule follow-up.
[00:09:18] Elena (Redwood CSM): i'll set a 30 minute follow-up for week of 11/10 and send calendar invites to your team.
[00:09:24] [00:09:30] Jon: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[00:09:32] Priya: thanks everyone.
[00:09:35] [00:09:38] Meeting end — recording stopped.
